Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: p95 200ms is optimistic but our product team insists on sub-250ms for the chat use case (we can accept p95 <= 250ms). p99 can be relaxed during spikes.
- Streaming: yes, token-level streaming is required for conversational UX. We currently open one streaming connection per active session; average session concurrency during business hours is ~60 but marketing campaigns can push that to ~120 for 5–10 minute windows.
- Request size: average prompt + response is ~600 tokens. We will batch at the client only for non-interactive async features; interactive chat should be single-request streaming.
- Connection pooling: our front end uses HTTP/1.1 keep-alive with a pool of ~100 connections per node. We expect multiple front-end nodes behind a load balancer.

Procurement note: procurement@acme.com needs the quota numbers and a simple doc to justify Dedicated versus Hosted. If you can include indicative pricing for both options in the proposal, that will speed review.

Hi Jared — thanks for the details, this helps. Short answers below plus an initial quota proposal attached.

Latency & hosting recommendation:
- p95 <= 250ms for ~600-token average payloads and token-level streaming is achievable on Dedicated with simple tuning; hosted plans may hit the target depending on region and load but are not SLA-backed for p95 under sustained 120 concurrency without reserved capacity.

Concurrency & rate-limits (initial proposal):
- Option A (Hosted, burst-enabled): baseline quota 100 concurrent streaming connections, 400 req/sec aggregate, with a 2x burst window (up to 200 concurrent for short periods) and automatic fair-share throttling. Intended for low-commit, faster onboarding.
- Option B (Dedicated): reserved pool sized for 150 concurrent streaming connections, 600 req/sec, predictable latency with capacity isolation, and agreed fallback to 50% capacity if underlying hardware maintenance occurs. Includes SLA for p95 latency.

Connection handling guidance:
- We recommend HTTP/2 for streaming to reduce connection count per client; if HTTP/1.1 keep-alive must be used, increase keep-alive timeout and configure client pools of 60–80 connections per node rather than 100 to avoid head-of-line limits on the platform side.
- Client retry: exponential backoff with capped retries (3 attempts) and jitter. For streaming disconnects, retry logic should re-establish a new streaming session and resume where feasible.

Pricing notes (indicative):
- Hosted (Option A): metered pricing with small premium for burst capability — see attached PDF for ballpark monthly cost at your projected usage.
- Dedicated (Option B): monthly reserved capacity commitment with lower per-token cost and SLA credits available.

2) Marissa: I'll finalize the numbers for procurement and include the HubSpot deal link + DocuSign placeholders so procurement@acme.com can start review.

Hi all — quick technical follow-up with recommended settings that should map to both Hosted and Dedicated options.

Recommended server-side settings:
- Keep-alive / connection pooling: prefer HTTP/2 multiplexing to allow a single connection per client to carry multiple streams. If HTTP/1.1 is required, set idle keep-alive to 60s and limit max connections per client IP to 80 to avoid queue buildup on load balancers.
- Concurrency model: use a token-bucket per-customer for concurrent streaming connections with a small global fair-share fallback. Example: bucket size = 150, refill rate = 5 tokens/sec (smooths bursts).
- Request throttling: soft limit at 90% of reserved concurrency with 429 responses including Retry-After and a short backoff window; hard limit at 100% to preserve p95 SLOs.
- Long-lived streams: track active sessions and implement idle timeouts (10 minutes) with a reconnect suggestion in the client for session resumption.

Operational notes:
- We'll need a short runbook for procurement showing how bursts are handled (auto-burst vs. throttling) and what monitoring/alerts we'll provide (active connections, token refill metrics, rejection rates). I can draft that and attach to the HubSpot deal.

Proposed immediate action:
- Marissa: share the draft runbook + quota pdf with procurement@acme.com and propose a 30-minute call next week to lock down Dedicated sizing if they prefer that route.

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the token-bucket math.
